research_progress.source_confidence_semantics: Heuristic official-source research confidence only. Current GOV.UK/DfT, National Highways and Active Travel England material checked on 25 July 2026. Strategic-road-network policy, transport statements/assessments, travel plans, statutory-consultee thresholds and active-travel design guidance remain at their published planning and design scope. They are not parcel highway-access approvals, junction capacity results, road-adoption agreements, traffic forecasts or Future Growth score accuracy.

source_facts.fact: Planning Practice Guidance says significant transport-generating development should be supported by a Transport Statement or Assessment and a Travel Plan, with significance judged case by case.
source_facts.gate: A generic threshold or document requirement is not a traffic-capacity result or planning outcome.

source_facts.fact: DfT Circular 01/2022 sets out how National Highways engages with plan-making and decision-taking for proposals affecting the strategic road network.
source_facts.gate: National Highways engagement or advice is not the local planning authority's final planning decision.

source_facts.fact: ATE is a statutory consultee on defined large planning applications, including 150 dwellings or more, over 7,500 square metres floorspace, or 5 hectares or more, and since 25 March 2026 is a specific consultation body for new-system local plans and supplementary plans.
source_facts.gate: Consultation threshold does not mean objection or approval.

source_facts.fact: ATE's design material brings together existing policy and guidance and explicitly does not replace NPPF or PPG.
source_facts.gate: ATE design guidance is not a parcel approval or highway adoption standard by itself.

source_facts.fact: DfT guidance provides best-practice accessibility and cycle-infrastructure design principles.
source_facts.gate: Design guidance values do not prove a proposed site's geometry, safety or compliance unless applied to actual drawings and conditions.

source_facts.fact: 2026 local transport plan guidance emphasizes accessibility and use of national design guidance while detailed legislative changes remain subject to their own commencement.
source_facts.gate: LTP policy is strategic evidence and not a parcel transport capacity or access right.

official_measurement_examples.name: ATE statutory development threshold dwellings
official_measurement_examples.fact: ATE statutory-consultee threshold includes development of 150 dwellings or more.

official_measurement_examples.name: ATE statutory floorspace threshold
official_measurement_examples.fact: ATE threshold includes development over 7,500 square metres of floorspace.

official_measurement_examples.name: ATE statutory site-area threshold
official_measurement_examples.fact: ATE threshold includes development of 5 hectares or more in site area.

official_measurement_examples.name: ATE local-plan role date
official_measurement_examples.fact: ATE states that from 25 March 2026 it became a specific consultation body for local plans and supplementary plans under the new plan-making system.

official_measurement_examples.name: SRN scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: Circular 01/2022 applies to trunk motorways and all-purpose trunk roads in England and not generally to the Major Road Network except at SRN junctions.

official_measurement_examples.name: Transport assessment significance
official_measurement_examples.fact: PPG requires case-by-case judgement of whether development generates significant transport movement.

official_measurement_examples.name: LTN 1/20 status
official_measurement_examples.fact: LTN 1/20 is DfT guidance for high-quality safe cycle infrastructure and does not itself approve a development design.

official_measurement_examples.name: Inclusive Mobility status
official_measurement_examples.fact: DfT describes Inclusive Mobility as best-practice guidance for accessible pedestrian and transport infrastructure.

core_rules: Transport Statement requirement is not a transport-impact conclusion
Transport Assessment requirement is not evidence of severe highway impact
Travel Plan requirement is not proof modal-shift targets will be achieved
case-by-case significance must not be replaced by a universal trip threshold
trip generation must not be fabricated without scheme inputs and method
traffic-flow baseline must not be inferred from road class alone
junction capacity must not be inferred from map proximity
highway-access geometry requires actual design evidence
visibility-splay compliance must not be guessed from aerial imagery
safe access is a planning judgement supported by evidence not a parcel binary label
local highway authority advice is not the LPA final planning decision
National Highways advice is not the LPA final planning decision
SRN policy must not be applied to every local road
Major Road Network and Strategic Road Network must remain distinct
new SRN connection policy must not be simplified to an automatic prohibition without policy context
plan-stage infrastructure identification is not planning permission
pre-application transport advice is not formal consultation response
formal consultation response is not planning permission
ATE statutory-consultee threshold is not an objection threshold
ATE consultation is not ATE approval of the whole planning application
ATE local-plan role is distinct from development-management casework
ATE design toolkit is guidance and not a statutory permission
Planning for Active Places does not supersede NPPF or PPG
LTN 1/20 is guidance and not a site-specific safety audit
Inclusive Mobility is design guidance and not proof an existing route is accessible
Manual for Streets guidance must not be represented as an adopted local highway standard without evidence
active-travel route existence does not prove development access is adequate
pedestrian access does not prove vehicular access
cycle-route proximity does not prove safe connection can be delivered
public transport proximity does not prove service capacity or frequency
bus-stop location is not evidence of service permanence
parking guidance does not establish a parcel parking requirement without local policy and proposal context
on-street parking design guidance is not a legal parking right
road width from mapping must not be treated as surveyed carriageway width
speed-limit sign or mapped limit is not measured operating speed
traffic-calming guidance is not evidence measures exist on site
junction design guidance is not a junction capacity assessment
crossing guidance is not evidence a crossing is deliverable at a specific location
barrier guidance is not evidence existing barriers meet accessibility standards
active-travel consultation does not replace road-safety audit where required
road-safety audit is not planning permission
section 278 agreement is distinct from planning permission
section 38 road-adoption agreement is distinct from planning permission
planning condition requiring highway works is not evidence those works are complete
delivery of transport mitigation must not be assumed from a planning obligation
strategic transport investment announcement is not completed local infrastructure
NO_DATA must not be converted into no transport constraint
no parcel highway approval transport-capacity result or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
